note: Text at top of p. 31 is the end of the ἄνθρωπος entry continued from p. 30 ('(see under υἱός), indicating a human being...'), not ἀνθύπατος; the ἀνθύπατος entry itself is entry 462.

text: ἀνθύπατος (pro consule, proconsul), a proconsul, a title applied to the governor of a senatorial province under the Empire, such as Cyprus (Ac. xiii 7, 8, 12), Achaia (Ac. xviii 12), and Asia (Ac. xix 38, where the plural is general and does not mean that there were more than one at a time). The word means originally one with the rank and insignia of a consul (i. e. the chief Roman magistrate), but was later applied to those who had not yet held the office of consul as well as to those who had.
ἀνίημι, I let go, loosen, release, give up.
gloss: I let go, loosen, release, give up

text: ἄνιπτος, unwashed.
Ἄννα (the aspirated form Ἅννα, favoured by W-H, is contradicted by the evidence of the versions), Anna, a prophetess, who visited the infant Jesus.
gloss: Anna, a prophetess, who visited the infant Jesus
note: Lemma Ἅννα (NT count 1) is Anna the prophetess; current_text had the following entry Ἄννας (Annas, high priest). Souter prints the headword with smooth breathing.

text: ἀνόητος, senseless (in Gal. iii 1 pathos is behind the use of the word, according to Ramsay, Historical Commentary, pp. 308 ff., and it describes a state of culture unworthy of the Romanized Galatians).
ἄνοια, senselessness.
ἀνοικοδομέω, I rebuild, build up (what has fallen or been razed to the ground): sometimes merely I build.
ἄνοιξις, opening (abstr.).
ἀνόμως, without law.
ἀνορθόω, I make upright (straight) again, I rear again, restore.
gloss: I make upright (straight) again, I rear again, restore

text: ἀνόσιος, regarding nothing as holy.
ἀνοχή, forbearance; suspense or delay (of punishment).
ἀνταγωνίζομαι, I struggle against.
ἀντάλλαγμα, an exchange, purchasing price.
ἀνταναπληρόω, I fill up in place of some one else.
gloss: I fill up in place of some one else

text: ἀνταπόδομα, a gift in return (for another), a return, a recompense.
gloss: a gift in return (for another), a return, a recompense

text: ἀνταπόδοσις, orig. abstr., giving in return, but in Col. iii 24 practically = ἀνταπόδομα.
ἀνταποκρίνομαι, I give a hostile answer.
ἀντέχομαι, I hold fast (firmly) to.
ἀντιβάλλω, I throw at in opposition (or quasi-opposition), I exchange (words) with; perhaps, I compare.
gloss: I throw at in opposition (or quasi-opposition)

text: ἀντιδιατίθεμαι, I am adversely affected against, I oppose.
gloss: I am adversely affected against, I oppose

text: ἀντίθεσις, a proposition, tenet, opinion advanced by one party against another.
ἀντικαθίστημι: 2 aor. I stoutly resisted.
ἀντικαλέω, I invite in return.
ἄντικρυς, right opposite, off (nautical sense).
ἀντιλαμβάνομαι, I lay hold of (in order to help), I aid (succour); I take in hand (lit. and met.), I undertake; I partake of, enjoy, 1 Tim. vi 2.
gloss: I lay hold of (in order to help), I aid (succour)

text: ἀντίλημψις, a lending a hand to, a helping (cf. ἀντιλαμβάνομαι, both being often used in petitions).
gloss: a lending a hand to, a helping

text: ἀντιλογία, contradiction, dispute.
ἀντιλοιδορέω, I abuse in return, I give abuse for abuse.
gloss: I abuse in return, I give abuse for abuse

text: ἀντίλυτρον, a stronger form of λύτρον, a ransom.
note: Gloss omits the roman-type note 'a stronger form of λύτρον'.

text: ἀντιμετρέω, I measure in return, I give equivalent measure, Lk. vi 38 (text doubtful).
gloss: I measure in return, I give equivalent measure

text: ἀντιμισθία, a reward, recompense (a more emphatic expression than the simple μισθός).
Ἀντιοχεύς, an Antiochian, an inhabitant of (Syrian) Antioch.
gloss: an Antiochian, an inhabitant of (Syrian) Antioch

text: ἀντιπαρέρχομαι, I pass opposite, on the opposite side of the road.
gloss: I pass opposite, on the opposite side of the road

text: Ἀντίπας (Ἀντείπας, Ἀντίφας, a pet form of Ἀντίπατρος), Antipas, a Christian martyr of Pergamum.
gloss: Antipas, a Christian martyr of Pergamum

text: Ἀντιπατρίς, Antipatris, a town, where was a Roman colony, on the road between Caesarea and Jerusalem.
ἀντίπερα, opposite.
ἀντιπίπτω, I fall foul of; I resist, oppose.
ἀντιστρατεύομαι, I campaign against, war against.
ἀντίτυπος (from τύπος, impress, impression left by a die), typical of, representing by type (or pattern), corresponding to: neut., as noun, an image.
gloss: typical of, representing by type (or pattern)

text: ἀντίχριστος, antichrist, either one who puts himself in the place of or the enemy (opponent) of the Messiah, a figure first appearing in the N.T., identified with various historical persons: the plur., of many such, in 1 John ii 18.
ἀντλέω, I draw (generally water from a deep well in the ground); perhaps, I draw out, John ii 9.
ἄντλημα, a pail attached to a rope, by which it is let down into a well.
gloss: a pail attached to a rope

text: ἀντοφθαλμέω, I face (lit. ‘I present my eye to’); I resist.
ἄνυδρος, waterless.
ἀνυπότακτος, unsubjected, unruly.
ἄνω (adv.), up, above; ἕως ἄνω, up to the top, up to the brim, John ii 7; τὰ ἄνω, things above, heaven, the heavenly region: see ἀνώτερον.
ἀνωτερικός, upper, higher-lying (the high central plateau of Asia Minor in contrast to the road through the valley).
ἀνώτερον (compar. of ἄνω, q. v.), (a) higher, to a more honourable place (at the dinner-table), Lk. xiv 10; (b) (superius) previously, in an earlier passage (of the book), above.
gloss: higher, to a more honourable place

text: ἀνωφελής, useless, unprofitable (perhaps also with the further idea, harmful, as in Plato).
ἀξίνη, axe.
ἀόρατος, unseen, invisible.
ἀπάγχομαι, I choke, strangle, hang myself.
ἀπαίδευτος, untrained, uneducated, showing a want of training or education.
ἀπαίρω, I take away, remove.
ἀπαιτέω (requiro), I ask back, or I ask what is my due.
ἀπαλγέω (lit. I cease to feel [my] pain), I am past feeling, cease to care (suggesting sometimes despair, sometimes recklessness), I become callous.
gloss: I am past feeling, cease to care

text: ἀπαλλάσσω, I free (a person) from (anything); oftener in the middle voice, I am released from, I am rid of (a person or thing).
ἀπαλλοτριόομαι, lit. I am being alienated from: the perf. pcpl. pass. is practically a noun = aliens.
ἁπαλός, tender.
ἀπαντάω, I meet.
ἀπάντησις, the act of meeting; εἰς ἀπάντησιν, to meet (a phrase seemingly almost technical for the reception of a newly arrived official).
ἀπαράβατος, inviolate, inviolable.
ἀπαρασκεύαστος, unprepared.
ἀπαρτισμός, setting up, erection; hence completion.
ἀπατάω (becoming obsolete in most countries), I deceive, cheat.
ἀπάτη (deceit, deception, or more probably, according to a Hellenistic sense), pleasure in Mk. iv 19 (= Mt. xiii 22, cf. Lk. viii 14), 2 Pet. ii 13.
note: Souter's first meanings stand in brackets; he prefers 'pleasure' for the passages cited.

text: ἀπάτωρ, without (recorded) father, of unknown father.
ἀπαύγασμα, a light flashing forth (from), radiation, gleam.
gloss: a light flashing forth (from), radiation, gleam

text: ἀπειλέω (apparently going out of popular speech), I threaten.
ἀπειλή, threatening, a threat.
ἀπεῖπον: in middle, ἀπειπάμην, I have renounced.
ἀπείραστος, untried, inexperienced (c. gen. = in); or untempted (c. gen. = to).
ἄπειρος (from πεῖρα), inexperienced (in), without experience (of), unacquainted (with).
ἀπεκδύομαι (probably coined by Paul), I put off (as a garment) from myself, I throw off.
gloss: I put off (as a garment) from myself, I throw off

text: ἀπέκδυσις (probably coined by Paul), a putting off (as of a garment), a casting off.
gloss: a putting off (as of a garment), a casting off

text: ἀπελαύνω, I drive away.
ἀπελεγμός, refutation, rejection; hence disrepute.
ἀπελεύθερος, a freedman, one who has been a slave but has been manumitted by his master.
Ἀπελλῆς, Apelles, a Christian (man) in Rome.
ἀπελπίζω (ἀφελπίζω), I despair: in Lk. vi 35, if μηδέν be the correct reading, μηδὲν ἀφελπίζοντες must be translated, despairing not at all, if μηδένα ἀφ., despairing of no one.
ἀπέναντι, over against, opposite; in view of, in presence of.
ἀπέραντος, unaccomplished, unending, endless.
ἀπερισπάστως, without distraction, without being distracted.
ἀπερίτμητος, uncircumcised; hence practically unclean; met. used of rankness, want of restraint.
ἁπλότης (simplicitas, sinceritas), singleness of mind, sincerity.
ἁπλοῦς (simplex), single: of the eye, directed towards one object.
ἁπλῶς, singly, simply: in James i 5 either graciously or unreservedly, without reserve.
ἀποβαίνω (I go away), (a) I disembark; (b) ἀποβαίνειν εἰς, to result in, to end in.
note: Gloss skips the bracketed literal sense '(I go away)'.

text: ἀποβάλλω, I cast away, I cast off: I lose, Heb. x 35.
gloss: I cast away, I cast off

text: ἀποβλέπω, I look away from one thing to another, I turn my attention to.
gloss: I look away from one thing to another

text: ἀπόβλητος, worthy to be cast away, worthless.
gloss: worthy to be cast away, worthless

text: ἀποβολή, a casting away, a loss.
ἀπογίνομαι (denascor) (opposite of γίνομαι: therefore, I go out of being, I cease to be), with the dat., I die away from.
note: Gloss skips the bracketed etymological sense 'I go out of being, I cease to be'.

text: ἀπογραφή, an enrolment, a census-taking, in which particulars not only of the persons but also of their property were generally given on the census-papers. The system began 10–9 B.C., and such an enrolment took place every fourteen years.
ἀπογράφομαι, I enrol myself (for the census); hence Heb. xii 23, in another connexion.
note: Souter's headword is the middle ἀπογράφομαι.

text: ἀποδείκνυμι, (a) I show off, display, exhibit, 1 Cor. iv 9; (b) I make good, demonstrate, Ac. xxv 7; (c) I make out (to be so and so), proclaim (to be), 2 Thess. ii 4; (d) I designate, nominate, appoint, Ac. ii 22.
ἀπόδειξις, display, exhibition (abstr.); the ordinary sense is proof.
ἀποδεκατόω, (a) as ἀποδεκατεύω; (b) c. acc. pers. I take a tenth part from.
gloss: I take a tenth part from
note: Sense (a) is only a cross-reference (as ἀποδεκατεύω); gloss is from (b).

text: ἀπόδεκτος, worthy to be received (welcomed), acceptable, welcome.
ἀποδημέω (ἀπό from, δῆμος parish), I am away from my parish, I am away from home, I am absent.
gloss: I am away from my parish, I am away from home

text: ἀπόδημος (see ἀποδημέω), away from home.
ἀποδιορίζω (I make a [logical] distinction), I make an (invidious) distinction.
ἀποδοχή (properly reception, welcome, of guests), acceptance, appreciation, approbation.
ἀπόθεσις, a putting off, a laying down.
gloss: a putting off, a laying down

text: ἀποθησαυρίζω, I store up, treasure up.
ἀποθλίβω (lit. I rub), I jostle.
ἀποκαραδοκία (perhaps coined by Paul), eager expectation.
ἀποκαταλλάσσω, I reconcile.
ἀποκατάστασις, re-establishment, restoration.
ἀπόκειμαι, I have been put away, I am stored.
gloss: I have been put away, I am stored

text: ἀποκεφαλίζω, I behead.
ἀποκλείω, I shut.
ἀπόκριμα (rescriptum), an answer (of God to the apostle's appeal, preserved in his heart).
ἀπόκρισις (rare in N.T. times), answering, answer.
ἀποκρύπτω, I hide away, conceal.
ἀπόκρυφος, hidden away, secret.
ἀποκυέω, I bring forth, give birth to (a child), a medical or physical word, marking the close of pregnancy.
gloss: I bring forth, give birth to (a child)

text: ἀποκυλίω, I roll (trans.) away from.
ἀπόλαυσις, the faculty or experience of enjoyment.
gloss: the faculty or experience of enjoyment

text: ἀπολείπω, I leave behind: in Heb. iv 6 ἀπολείπεται is impers. (= restat), it remains.
Ἀπολλύων (properly pres. pcpl. of ἀπολλύω, cf. ἀπόλλυμι), The Destroying One, a Greek translation of the Hebr. Abaddon.
Ἀπολλωνία, Apollonia, a city of Macedonia.
ἀπολούω, I wash off; mid. I wash away (my sins, in baptism).
note: Souter's headword is the active ἀπολούω; the middle sense is 'I wash away'.

text: ἀμομάσσομαι, I wipe off myself (on to another).
gloss: I wipe off myself (on to another)
note: Headword is misprinted ἀμομάσσομαι (μ for π) on the page; transcribed as printed.

text: ἀπονέμω, I apportion, render (as due).
ἀπονίπτω, I wash dirt off.
ἀποπίπτω, I fall away (from), I fall off.
gloss: I fall away (from), I fall off

text: ἀποπλανάω, I cause to wander astray: 1 Tim. vi 10 (aor. pass.), I have wandered away.
ἀποπλέω, I sail away.
ἀποπνίγω, (a) I choke, drown; (b) I stop the growth of.
ἀπορία, state of difficulty, distress.
ἀπορίπτω, I throw away from, I throw overboard.
gloss: I throw away from, I throw overboard

text: ἀπορφανίζω, I separate from some one.
ἀποσκίασμα, either a shadow cast by an object, or a faint image or copy of an object.
gloss: a shadow cast by an object

text: ἀποσπάω, lit. I wrench away from, I drag away; but perhaps sometimes in the well-attested weakened sense, I withdraw.
gloss: I wrench away from, I drag away

text: ἀποστασία, a revolting, revolt, especially religious apostasy.
ἀποστάσιον, divorce.
ἀποστεγάζω, I unroof, take the roof off.
gloss: I unroof, take the roof off

text: ἀποστερέω, I deprive one of something, I rob; absol. in Mk. x 19 (1 Cor. vii 5).
gloss: I deprive one of something, I rob

text: ἀποστολή, commission, duty of ἀπόστολος (apostle), apostleship.
ἀποστοματίζω (literary, from ἀπὸ στόματος), I draw out by questioning.
ἀποστρέφω (seems mostly literary) (trans.), (a) I turn away (from); (b) (mid.) I turn myself away from; (c) (metaph.) I pervert, Lk. xxiii 14.
ἀποστυγέω, I shrink from (with horror).
ἀποσυνάγωγος, away from the synagogue, expelled the synagogue, excommunicated.
gloss: away from the synagogue, expelled the synagogue

text: ἀποτελέω, I complete, accomplish, Lk. xiii 32; I form fully, James i 15.
ἀποτινάσσω, I shake off.
ἀποτίνω, I repay, pay what is due (by way of punishment or fine).
gloss: I repay, pay what is due

text: ἀποτολμάω (literary), I break out boldly.
ἀποτομία (lit. sheerness, of a rock), peremptoriness, inexorableness, harshness, severity.
ἀποτόμως, sharply, severely.
ἀποτρέπομαι, I turn myself away from.
ἀπουσία, absence.
ἀποφεύγω, I flee from.
ἀποφθέγγομαι, I utter forth, speak out.
ἀποφορτίζομαι, I discharge my cargo.
ἀπόχρησις, using up.
ἀποχωρέω, I go away, depart.
ἀποχωρίζομαι, I separate myself from.
ἀποψύχω, I faint or I die.
Ἄππιος, Appius (censor 312 B. C.), after whom the township Appi Forum on the Appian Way, 43 Roman miles from Rome, was named.
note: Souter's headword is the nominative Ἄππιος (lemma is the genitive Ἀππίου, as in Ἀππίου Φόρον).

text: ἀπρόσιτος, unapproachable.
ἀπρόσκοπος, (free from hurt or harm, hence) not offending, not causing offence, blameless.
gloss: not offending, not causing offence, blameless

text: ἀπροσωπολήμπτως (literary and Jewish), without any preference (undue favour, partiality) for a person.
gloss: without any preference (undue favour, partiality) for a person

text: ἄπταιστος (literary and rare), not stumbling.
Ἀπφία, Ἀφφία, Apphia, a Christian lady of Colossae, either wife or sister of Philemon.
gloss: Apphia, a Christian lady of Colossae

text: ἀπωθέομαι, I push (thrust) away from myself.
